ledger_entries.metric: C2 gas family grid-delivered TWh (preliminary 2025 vintage)
ledger_entries.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (EIA-930 gas-vs-OTHER fold-in + preliminary-vintage incompleteness)
ledger_entries.reason: 2025 is a preliminary EIA-923 vintage — per-class actuals are incomplete (audit 2026-07-04: 13/30 prior CC_REGULAR plants missing, 57% reporting; gas family incomplete). The scorer falls back to the EIA-930 grid gas cell, which INCLUDES geothermal+biomass (~5.2 TWh); the correction formula under-corrects because the preliminary vintage's per-class cells are incomplete. Same categorization issue documented for the complete-vintage years, where the per-class C1 gate PASSES under the load-scaled band. When the full 2025 vintage reconciles, the per-class gate replaces this family fallback. NOT closable by adjusting model dispatch.

ledger_entries.classification: MODEL MISS (winter fuel-inventory scarcity rent / reserve scarcity)
ledger_entries.reason: The energy-only LP caps the cold-hour price at the dual-fuel oil-parity (~$258/MWh). The post-solve ORDC scarcity overlay (ISO-NE-grounded LOLP curve: VOLL $2000 = Tariff III.1.10.1A offer cap, MCL 1200 MW ~ Millstone 3, sigma 900 MW = PAF Study 2022) fires and modifies econ_prices for capacity economics but does not change the persisted LP prices. The fast-start tranche pricing added in this run lifts the summer-evening and shoulder peak pricing but cannot produce >$300 cold-snap hours — that scarcity rent is the finite winter fuel INVENTORY the LP prices as an unlimited flow. Closable only via the documented winter fuel-inventory / seasonal-reliability build (docs/multi-iso/neiso-winter-fuel-inventory-plan-2026-07.md), NEVER via an offer adder tuned to the tail.

ledger_entries.magnitude: model $31.98 vs actual $35.70 (-10.4%; was -8.3% under the retired, unreproducible keeper)
ledger_entries.classification: OPEN ROOT CAUSE (honest cost of killing ERCOT offer-band leakage, commit 0c6c833 / rule #25 — NOT this run's CT scrub)
ledger_entries.reason: neiso-47's price pass (-4.6/-2.3%) was partly produced by ERCOT-fitted CT_PEAKER/CC_CHP/ST_GAS econ bands that leaked cross-ISO into _NEISO_OFFER_CURVE; commit 0c6c833 killed that leakage (rule #25), de-leaking those bands to neutral 1.0. Model clearing prices fell ~$2/MWh as a result. This CT-floor scrub is price-neutral (A/B dw-LMP +$0.04). Closable ONLY by grounding real NEISO-measured CT/CC_CHP/ST_GAS part-load HR spreads (rule #1 second-step calibration), never by re-introducing the ERCOT-leaked bands (rule #25). ADDENDUM (neiso-50, this bundle): on top of the pre-existing 0c6c833 de-leak gap above, this bundle also loses the retired keeper's HQ_import zonal price separation (never present in any committed commit -- see governance.note) -- roughly -$0.75/MWh (2023), -$0.31/MWh (2024) of the total gap is that lost, unreproducible, non-mechanistic separation, not a new structural regression.
